method: Personally inspected full actual native exact source/result pairs, before phone and root returned-image verdict. Existing source observations and intended surface targets known. F1 success not inferred from its phase label.

observations: Dense red grass/web carpet becomes broad burgundy leaf groups; petal glints and cross-vein noise reduce while translucent charcoal membranes, silver mouth, thorn/root direction and glasshouse depth remain.
Adult face, anatomical RIGHT saber/LEFT guard and walking pose retain appeal. No material new structural loss observed; existing root-lock uncertainty remains.
Petal vein mesh, tiny sparkle and foreground red blades become broader translucent membrane/value groups; mouth rim, planted root at door, enormous scale and heroine stance remain.
Face and RIGHT saber/LEFT guard preserved. Less glitter makes it more somber but retains the specific delicate bloom material; no material new structural regression observed.
Foreground tangled red blades, membrane mesh and pinprick petals simplify; cut gap, falling root fragments, tipped flower and follow-through silhouette remain readable.
Face slightly smoother and root fibers less intricate, but no major pose or consequence regression observed. Wrong sword arm and stump/door geography remain unchanged limitations.
Red ground tangles, fallen bloom mesh, shawl/skirt micro-patterns and frame scratches reduce while boot on loose root, open door, Neris palm and fallen flower persist.

Faces remain appealing, though smoother. Coat-tail notches are more explicit/differently drawn in F1 than the weak source edge: do not claim exact damage preservation or credit this as an authorized structural fix. No major change to rescue geometry observed.
entries.display_recommendation: Prefer F1 pending phone, with local damage-detail redraw disclosed.

observations: Concrete streaks and rippled white/magenta chatter become broad vertical wall washes and grouped reflection bands. Huge gate/arch, two adults, held notebook/coat and upright single C-pole remain.
Water remains high contrast but less fragmented; dry-brush edge character and slab construction survive. No material new structural regression observed.
Footprint and two pointing hands are easier to isolate against broad pale concrete; coat scratches and reflection splinters group into larger dry-brush shapes.
Single print, notebook/coat placement, two black gloves, upright C-pole and stern adult faces persist. Some low-contrast concrete grain remains; no new plot or anatomy regression observed.
Strong reduction of wall/coat scratches and white/magenta water chatter; still empty pool, hovering bare LEFT hand, black RIGHT glove, removed glove and separate C-pole persist.

This is a stronger rendering shift than FL01/03: faces and black coat become clean shaded contours, walls/sky much smoother and less dry-brushed. Adult identities remain, but source weathered/raw character is reduced. Do not describe this as no style change.
entries.display_recommendation: F1 has a clear focus gain; provisional preference F1 with material/medium tradeoff, pending phone comparison.

observations: Coat, pavement and distant water noise reduce into broad ink/wash masses; empty disturbed pool still has explicit circular ripples, with notebook/C-pole and elbow restraint unchanged.

Face shadows are smoother but adult concern remains. Source wrong glove-side assignment persists. F preserves the large disturbance rather than erasing a story cue; no material new structural regression observed.
Body scuffs and white water/stone chatter simplify into broad umbrella panels and reflection groups; rib hinges, dripping mouth, wet trunk connection and initial two-adult dry ledge remain.
Large scale and menace survive; two grips and C-head-above/butt-to-threat pose are preserved, with no claim of contact. No material new structural regression observed.
